{{Vanilla|Turtle Scute}}
{{Infobox auto}}
A '''Divine Fragment''' is a rare magic material that replaces the {{MCW|Turtle Scute|turtle scute}}. It comes from breaking [[spawner]]s and defeating powerful mobs, and is needed for late-game items: [[Adamant Alloy]], [[Electrum Alloy]], [[Crystal Heart]]s, [[Bedrock Buster]]s, [[Eye of Ender|eyes of ender]] and the [[Prayer of Prometheus]]. Nine fragments make a [[Divine Favor]].

== Obtaining ==
Divine fragments cannot be farmed from ordinary mobs. The developer's video describes them as the pack's main answer to mob grinders: every spawner broken gives one, so a spawner is worth more broken than built into a farm.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=I wanted to have a way to disincentivize mob grinders and I think this one mechanic does a lot of the heavy lifting. You could make a simple mob grinder, but the divine fragment is staring you in the face. If you want to get to the end, you need that fragment.}}</ref>

=== Sources ===
{{Sources}}
Every source uses the same fragment, which has rare (aqua) rarity and an enchantment glint.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/treasure/divine_fragment.json}}</ref> Spawners always drop exactly one: Fortune has no effect on them.

=== Crafting ===
{{Recipes}}
A Divine Favor can be broken down into 9 fragments, and 9 fragments craft a Divine Favor.

=== Trading ===
A master-level [[Mouthpiece]] sells one Divine Fragment for 2 [[Crystal Heart]]s and an echo shard.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/villager_trade/librarian/5/crystal_heart.json}}</ref>

== Usage ==
{{Uses}}
One fragment and one [[Stabilized Estus]] make 16 eyes of ender, enough to fill an {{MCW|End Portal|end portal}}. A fragment and a {{MCW|Trial Key|trial key}} make an {{MCW|Ominous Trial Key|ominous trial key}}.

== Behavior ==
A Divine Fragment lying on the ground gives off small electric spark particles.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/timers/0_5/item_particles.mcfunction}}</ref>

The fragment is a turtle scute with rare rarity. Ordinary turtle scutes, such as those shed by baby turtles, are not kept: when a player outside Creative mode picks up a common-rarity scute, it is replaced with a [[Turtle Shellmet]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/remove_vanilla_items/turtle_scute.mcfunction}}</ref> The vanilla turtle shell recipe is removed.
